title: Event
description:
An immutable observed fact in the LAOCOON event log. Events are append-only and are never edited; a correction is a new compensating event. Everything else in the system (graphs, measures, the site) is a regenerable projection of this log.
`event_id` is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of `{event_type, payload}` and therefore excludes `observed_at`. Re-observing an unchanged fact produces the same `event_id`, so a re-crawl appends nothing. This is what keeps the log a stream of deltas rather than a daily snapshot.

event_id.description: SHA-256 over canonical JSON of {event_type, payload}. Idempotency key.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the event was written against.

observed_at.description: When the observation was made, not when the observed thing happened. Deliberately excluded from `event_id`.

ContentHash.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256, prefixed with its algorithm.

SenderId.description:
SHA-256 of the lowercased, trimmed RFC 5322 addr-spec of the sender. The plaintext address is never written to the public log; the address-to-id map lives in the gitignored `private/` directory.
The hash is unsalted on purpose: a participant can hash their own address and confirm exactly which rows describe them, which is required by the contestability commitment in PROBLEM.md section 8. It is not a bulk harvesting surface, which a plaintext column would be.

SourceRef.description: Where an observation came from. The crawler sits behind an interface; this records which implementation actually produced the fact.

mailbox.description: Mailbox path the observation was read from, when applicable.

MessageId.description: RFC 5322 msg-id with surrounding angle brackets and whitespace stripped. Case is preserved: msg-id comparison is case-sensitive in the local part.

MessageObserved.description: Structural facts about one message as seen in one mailbox. Message bodies are NOT stored here: only a digest and shape counts. The corpus is already published by the IETF; re-publishing it in this repository would add nothing and could not be undone, because the log is immutable.

uid.description: IMAP UID, unique and stable only within a given uid_validity.

uid_validity.description: IMAP UIDVALIDITY of the mailbox at observation time.

message_id.description: Null when the message carried no parseable Message-ID header.

in_reply_to.description: All msg-ids parsed from In-Reply-To, in header order.

references.description: All msg-ids parsed from References, in header order (root first).

sent_at.description: Date header parsed to ISO 8601 UTC; null when unparseable.

sent_at_raw.description: The Date header verbatim, so an unparseable date is auditable.

BodyShape.description: Mechanical shape of the plain-text body. Every field here is countable without judging the text. Whether a reply is substantive is a separate, model-derived record introduced in phase 3, never a field on this event.

quoted_lines.description: Lines matching the RFC 3676 quote prefix ">".

unquoted_lines.description: lines - quoted_lines - signature/attribution lines removed. New text written by this sender, counted rather than judged.

CrawlWindowCompleted.description: What one crawl actually covered. Emitted on every run, successful or not, so a gap in coverage is a visible fact instead of a silent absence. Every published figure must be able to cite the windows it rests on.

mode.description: incremental walks UIDs above the watermark; full re-examines the whole mailbox and can emit ObservationSuperseded.

mailbox_total.description: Messages the server reported present in the mailbox.

watermark_before.description: Highest UID already ingested before this run; null on first run.

failures.description: UIDs the crawl could not turn into an observation, and why.

ObservationSuperseded.description: A previously recorded observation no longer matches the source. The earlier event stays in the log untouched; this event is the correction. Projections must ignore any MessageObserved that a later event supersedes.
